name: Engaging Families
title: Engaging Families
answer: Engaging families means using AI to help schools understand family feedback, explain AI to parents, and support home learning, while keeping people in charge of judgment. It matters because families who understand the tools and feel heard become better partners in students' education. The school still decides which tools are shown and checks that AI summaries are fair.

sections.body: Family surveys produce useful feedback but open responses take time to read. A school can gather surveys with Google Forms and use AI features in spreadsheet tools to sort responses into themes. A staff member then reads a sample from each theme to confirm the grouping is fair. Those themes inform school planning. Parent AI nights and other engagement efforts can also use AI support, such as cultural calendars, volunteer coordination, and family learning activities sent home in the family's language.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, survey responses can be collected through Google Forms and grouped by AI features in spreadsheet tools. A staff member reviews a sample of responses in each theme to check fairness before the themes guide planning. Parent AI nights can show the tools students use, explain the rules, and answer questions, but only school approved tools should be demonstrated. Other work can use Google Forms and Google Sheets for volunteer coordination, a cultural calendar for holidays and observances, and family learning activities sent home in the family's language. The text does not give grade bands for these practices.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text provides no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It describes practical steps and intended benefits rather than research results. So this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: AI does not replace human review. A staff member must read a sample of responses in each theme to check that the grouping is fair. Only school approved tools should be shown at parent AI nights. The school keeps the decisions about which tools are approved, what rules are explained, and how themes guide planning. Families remain partners, not subjects of automated judgment.
